name: Phylogenetic signal and LIPA on the program tree
title: How much program growth runs in the family tree?
field: comparative biology and community ecology (phylogenetic signal)
what: Treats the program hierarchy as a family tree and measures, globally and per program, how much growth relatives share.
grade: well established (K, λ); LIPA promising but thin
pick_line: Measurement-error-corrected λ using each program's slope standard error, to split shared growth from noise.
data: SYNTHETIC mock ZBB budgets (Corning-like and Morgan Stanley-like); answer key used only for scoring
one: Noise hides most tree signal (λ 0.52 vs 1.22); relatives beat OLS growth by 7–14%; LIPA flags miss.

picture.la: Usual tool: growth by function, 51 boxes (MS-like)
picture.lb: Tree view: growth bars coloured by LIPA (MS-like)

findings.h: Noise hides most of the growth the tree explains.
findings.t: On the label tree (segment > subsegment > function > stated intent), Pagel's λ of per-program growth is 0.52 on observed actuals vs 1.22 on noise-free growth (Corning-like), and 0.78 vs 1.12 (MS-like). Blomberg's K falls 91% (4.54 → 0.40) and 64% (1.50 → 0.54). All four indices p = 0.001 (999 permutations).
findings.note: Standard comparison: ANOVA R² of slope on function is 0.45 vs 0.96 noise-free (Corning-like) and 0.59 vs 0.85 (MS-like). λ and K say the same thing in a form that also handles nested levels and gives per-node and per-program versions. λ > 1 is allowed by the estimator.

chart.la: Pagel's λ: true vs observed vs text tree

findings.h: Descriptions carry less growth signal than the labels.
findings.t: A tree from the descriptions (TF-IDF, average linkage; every sentence with numbers, dollars, actuals or budget words removed, about 40% of words) gives λ 0.35 (Corning-like) and 0.57 (MS-like) vs 0.52 and 0.78 on the label tree; K is not significant on the text tree (p = 0.46 and 0.15).
findings.note: The descriptions leak numeric history ("actuals have risen from $4.76 million…"); without the scrub the text tree would be measuring the numbers. On these mocks, the words add nothing beyond the categories they were generated from.

findings.h: Borrowing from relatives beats a per-program trend, but not a pooled ARDL.
findings.t: One-step walk-forward of last-year log growth: a relatives-weighted mean of last observed growth (patristic weights on the label tree) has RMSE 0.242 vs OLS trend 0.261 (−7.2%, Corning-like) and 0.225 vs 0.263 (−14.3%, MS-like); pre-registered bar −5% passed. Pooled ARDL(1): 0.244 and 0.217. "No change": 0.231 and 0.236. Per-program SARIMAX(1,0,0): 0.297, and diverged on some MS-like programs.
findings.note: Against noise-free growth the relatives' mean is best on the MS-like book (0.110 vs ARDL 0.137, OLS 0.139) but "no change" wins on the Corning-like book (0.103 vs 0.125). Not a forecasting method; the benchmark checks that borrowing is real.

findings.h: LIPA does not flag text-vs-numbers mismatches or category drift.
findings.t: "Says growth, actually declining": negative LIPA AUC 0.59 (Corning-like, 6 planted) and 0.53 (MS-like, 25) vs a plain OLS slope 0.74 and 0.65. Category drift (LIPA early minus late window): AUC 0.55 and 0.47 for any drift. One cell passed the pre-registered bar (MS-like "says transform, actually run": 0.71 vs best comparator 0.58), but the same type on the Corning-like book is 0.48; read as chance among 10 cells.
findings.note: LIPA multiplies a program's deviation by its relatives' deviation, so a program near the overall mean scores near zero even when it differs from its siblings (see the toy).

findings.h: LIPA finds planted co-moving groups, but a category-cell flag does as well.
findings.t: Programs with significant positive LIPA (like their relatives): 311 of 778 and 777 of 1,404. Share of them in a planted co-moving group: 0.49 and 0.41, vs 0.40 and 0.27 for the same number of largest own slopes; but flagging the most extreme function × intent cell means (either direction) gives 0.53 and 0.45.
findings.note: Added after seeing results (not pre-registered). The mocks place planted groups by archetype, so category cells are a strong baseline (the 11-18 STEM run found the same).
